citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022).
creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (University of California Los Angeles, Arizona State University, Allen Institute for AI)
description: ScienceQA is a large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question answering benchmark consisting of 21,208 questions with diverse science topics spanning natural science, social science, and language science. Questions are sourced from elementary and high school science curricula (grades 1–12) and most are annotated with corresponding lectures and explanations that serve as chain-of-thought reasoning annotations. The dataset includes multimodal contexts (images and text) and covers 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills.
name: ScienceQA
publisher: University of California Los Angeles / Allen Institute for AI (AI2)
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (each question in the human performance study was answered by 3 different AMT workers; each explanation evaluation batch was assigned to 3 workers)
rai:annotatorDemographics: For the human performance study, only AMT workers who hold a high school degree or higher and pass qualification examples were eligible. Workers needed to correctly answer 4 out of 5 exam examples to qualify.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was measured at 88.40% average accuracy on the test set. For generated explanation evaluation, human scores were determined by majority vote across 3 annotators. Annotators rated explanations on relevance, correctness, and completeness. 65.2% of GPT-3 (CoT) generated explanations met the gold standard (relevant, correct, and complete) by human evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) — used for human performance study and human evaluation of generated explanations. Expert annotators from IXL Learning curated the original dataset content.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge/background information for solving problems of a similar class. The explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. Incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts using a data exploration tool. The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20 (12,726 / 4,241 / 4,241 examples respectively).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is sourced from California Common Core Content Standards via IXL Learning, which may introduce geographic and curriculum bias toward California/US educational standards. The paper notes that 83.9% of questions have lectures and 90.5% have explanations, meaning a minority of questions lack these annotations. The dataset covers grades 1–12 but the majority of questions come from middle-level curriculum (grades 3–8), with only ~10% from high school (grades 9–12). Answer options were shuffled to avoid positional bias.
rai:dataCollection: Questions in ScienceQA are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid questions (those with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates) were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled to avoid patterns. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems sourced from IXL Learning (https://www.ixl.com/), an online K-12 education platform. Raw data consisted of science problems aligned with California Common Core Content Standards, containing questions, hints, images, answer options, answers, lectures, and solutions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal models fail to achieve satisfactory performance on ScienceQA, with a 20.07% gap between human performance and the best model for image-context questions. Image captions used as visual input lack fine-grained semantics and do not work well for diagrams. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only. The paper notes failure cases where models cannot understand multimodal inputs, lack domain-specific knowledge, or generate wrong chain-of-thought reasoning.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20 (12,726 / 4,241 / 4,241 examples respectively).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from downloaded science problems using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed (those with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates). If multiple correct answers applied, only one was kept. Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions so that special structures (tables, lists) are distinguishable from plain text. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ScienceQA is proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race. The dataset will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The authors adhere to the goal of AI for the common good, and any anti-social data points will be removed based on feedback. After careful examination, no improper content (pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias) was found.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal learning and multi-hop reasoning in AI systems; diagnosing multi-hop reasoning ability and interpretability of AI systems; developing chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models; K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems; few-shot and fine-tuning learning research with language models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 (available at https://huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) was used to generate captions for images in the dataset, with maximum caption length of 16, 4 beams, and maximum 512 output tokens. Sentence-BERT was used for automatic evaluation of generated explanations via cosine similarity of semantic embeddings.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content. It does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process; questions without context are handled by replacing context with an empty string, but this is an experimental detail not a collection gap.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described beyond the initial release.
